title: Spacial plotting
text: plot location postcodes ELAPSE geo-location required provided trough: pollutionFromBag() pollutionFromPc6(). function output spacial data geom column. Plotting data achieved geom_sf(), see block .
code: load(system.file("extdata/postcode100.rda", package = "postcodElapse"))  pc6 <- pollutionFromPc6(postcode100, "../../../data/cbs_pc6_2024.gpkg") #> Guessed db type to be: PC6 bag <- pollutionFromBag(postcode100, "../../../data/bag-light.gpkg") #> Guessed db type to be: BAG  ggplot() +   geom_spatraster(data = elapse$NO2FULL) +    geom_sf(data = pc6, aes(geometry = geom), fill = "purple", alpha = 0.7) +   geom_sf(data = bag, aes(geometry = geom), colour = "orange") +   scale_fill_grass_c() #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 500490 cells.

title: Spacial plotting
text: Due scale ELAPSE many situations hard visualize data. alleviate recommend creating inset plot marking location zoom main plot. postcodElapse provides helpers see block .  using geom_rectFeatrue() coord_zoomFeature() ensure subset entire rows using [12, ]. Additionally air pollution estimate always returned alpha numeric order.
code: library(ggpubr) #used to arrange plots into one figure.  main <- ggplot() +   geom_spatraster(data = elapse$NO2FULL) +    geom_sf(data = pc6, aes(geometry = geom), fill = "purple", alpha = 0.7) +   geom_sf(data = bag, aes(geometry = geom), colour = "orange", alpha = 0.7) +   scale_fill_grass_c(transform = "log10") +   geom_rectFeature(pc6[100, ], 5000) +   labs(fill = bquote("log"[10]~" Concentration NO"[2]~"µg/m"^3)) +   theme(legend.position = "top") #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 500490 cells.  inset <- ggplot() +   geom_spatraster(data = elapse$NO2FULL) +    geom_sf(data = pc6, aes(geometry = geom), fill = "purple", alpha = 0.7) +   geom_sf(data = bag, aes(geometry = geom), colour = "orange", alpha = 0.7) +   scale_fill_grass_c(transform = "log10") +   coord_zoomFeature(pc6[100, ]) #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 500490 cells.  fig <- ggarrange(main, inset, ncol = 2,                  common.legend = TRUE,                  legend.grob = get_legend(main))  annotate_figure(fig,                  fig.lab.pos = "bottom.left",                 fig.lab = "NO2 pollution in the Netherlands, with postcode location plotted. Orange is BAG purple is PC6.")

Linking locations ELAPSE air quality model. Calculate postcode-level air pollutant concentration estimates. vignette guide setting , running utilizing postcodElapse.

title: postcodElapse - Usage guide
text: described , geographic location area postcode required order estimate air pollutant concentrations. postcodElapse expects data provided GeoPackage (.gpkg) files, format commonly used storing spatial data. Currently, postcodElapse supports two GeoPackages: BAG (Basisregistratie Adressen en Gebouwen bag data set contains every building Netherlands location & postcode. Size 8GB PC6 (Postcode6)  provides geographic area every Dutch postcode. package assumes GeoPackages stored locally location accessible R session.

title: postcodElapse - Usage guide
text: estimate air pollutant concentration, call main function postcodElapse() postcode (can also vector) path relevant GeoPackage. example, BAG GeoPackage use. output structure identical using PC6; database path needs adjusting. postcodElapse() returns data frame row corresponds postcode. Columns include: postcode Number buildings postcode n. summary statistics (mean, minimum & maximum) pollutant extracted ELAPSE, concentration µg/m3. wish experiment lager sets postcodes, files postcode100.rda & postcode1000.rda available package’s extdata. See example.

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # You need to use this with a plot so the basics library(tidyverse) library(tidyterra) library(postcodElapse)  data <- pollutionFromBag("9726AC", "bag-light.gpkg")  elapse <- loadElapse()  # We are zooming in on the 3rd building. ggplot() +    geom_spatraster(data = elapse$NO2FULL) +    geom_sf(data = data, aes(geometry = geom), colour = "red") +    coord_zoomFeature(data[3, ]) # you must index with `[3, ]` the entire row is expected!  # On the 5th trough 10th buildings ggplot() +    geom_spatraster(data = elapse$NO2FULL) +    geom_sf(data = data, aes(geometry = geom), colour = "red") +    coord_zoomFeature(data[5:10, ]) } # }

what: Estimate air pollution concentrations in a postcode with BAG database. — pollutionFromBag
title: Estimate air pollution concentrations in a postcode with BAG database. — pollutionFromBag
text: Kadaster's Basisregistratie Adressen en Gebouwen database contains buildings Netherlands location postcode. pollutionFromBag() finds geo-location buildings part given postcodes. extracts air pollutant concentrations geo-locations ELAPSE. Returned pollution estimates every building wanted postcodes, including geo-location.

title: Estimate air pollution concentrations in a postcode with BAG database. — pollutionFromBag
code: pollutionFromBag(postcodes, bag_path, elapse_path, ...)

title: Estimate air pollution concentrations in a postcode with BAG database. — pollutionFromBag
text: postcodes string vector strings Containing Duch postcodes. bag string Path BAG database. elapse optional Path ELAPSE. (empty load internal ELAPSE)

title: Estimate air pollution concentrations in a postcode with BAG database. — pollutionFromBag
text: data.frame containing air pollution estimates geo-location buildings given postcodes

title: Estimate air pollution concentrations in a postcode with BAG database. — pollutionFromBag
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Basic usage pollutionFromBag("9726AC", "bag-light.gpkg")  # Plotting the location of all buildings, # I recommend you use tidyverse & tidyterra library(tidyverse) library(tidyterra) library(postcodElapse)  data <- pollutionFromBag("9726AC", "bag-light.gpkg")  elapse <- loadElapse()  ggplot() +    geom_spatraster(data = elapse$NO2FULL) +    geom_sf(data = data, aes(geometry = geom), colour = "red") } # }

what: Estimate air pollution concentrations in a postcode with PC6 database. — pollutionFromPc6
title: Estimate air pollution concentrations in a postcode with PC6 database. — pollutionFromPc6
text: Postcode6(PC6) CBS, contains geographic region every postcode Netherlands. pollutionFromPc6() query's geographic region given postcodes. Subsequently uses ELAPSE calculate average, minimum & maximum concentration every air pollutant region. addition collects amount buildings region.

title: Estimate air pollution concentrations in a postcode with PC6 database. — pollutionFromPc6
code: pollutionFromPc6(postcodes, pc6_path, elapse_path, ...)

title: Estimate air pollution concentrations in a postcode with PC6 database. — pollutionFromPc6
text: postcodes string vector strings Containing PC6 postcodes. pc6_path string Path Postcode6 database. elapse_path optional string Path ELAPSE database.

title: Estimate air pollution concentrations in a postcode with PC6 database. — pollutionFromPc6
text: simple feature collection. every postcode average, minimum & maximum air pollutant concentration. addition geographic area postcode.

title: Estimate air pollution concentrations in a postcode with PC6 database. — pollutionFromPc6
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # basic use pollutionFromPc6("9726AC", "cbs_pc6_2024.gpkg")  # Plotting the area's, I recommend you use tidyverse & tidyterra library(tidyverse) library(tidyterra) library(postcodElapse)  data <- pollutionFromPc6("9726AC", "cbs_pc6_2024.gpkg")  elapse <- loadElapse()  ggplot() +  geom_spatraster(data = elapse$NO2FULL) +  geom_sf(data = data, aes(geometry = geom), colour = "red") } # }

what: Estimate air pollutant concentraions for a given Dutch postcode. — postcodElapse
title: Estimate air pollutant concentraions for a given Dutch postcode. — postcodElapse
text: Estimates air pollutant concentration given Dutch postcodes. Using ELAPSE (included) postcode database (-included). Two postcode databases formatted Geopackage (.gpkg) supported Postcode6(PC6) Basisregistratie Adressen en Gebouwen(BAG) download one point database  argument location. PostcodElapse automatically guesses type argument, can set "PC6" "BAG".

title: Estimate air pollutant concentraions for a given Dutch postcode. — postcodElapse
code: postcodElapse(postcodes, database_path, database_type = "GUESS", elapse_path)

title: Estimate air pollutant concentraions for a given Dutch postcode. — postcodElapse
text: postcodes String containing Dutch postcode (1234AB) can also vector. elapse_path empty ELAPSE stored extdata used. Otherwise use one provided. database Path postcode database, see Postcode database . type Type postcode database, defaults "GUESS" postcodElapse fills type "BAG" Basisregistratie Adressen en Gebouwen "PC6" Postcode6.

title: Estimate air pollutant concentraions for a given Dutch postcode. — postcodElapse
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Estimate air pollution for postcode "8933DV" with Postcode6. postcodElapse("8933DV", "cbs_pc6_2024.gpkg")  # Estimate air pollution for multiple postcodes with BAG. postcodElapse(c("8933DV", "9713 GZ", "1071XX"), "bag-light.gpkg")  # Note postcodes are valid a long as they are four numbers followed by two letters. # In addition any spaces will be removed and non-capital letters will be capitalized. postcodElapse(c("8 9 3 3 DV", "9 713 Gz", "1071 xx"), "cbs_pc6_2024.gpkg") } # }
